advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Apply the built-in inward/outward direction inversion (INVERSE_RELATION) when recovering an overridden remote link type in _diff_link_removals, or restrict override recovery to symmetric relations only.
evidence: reverse is built config-unaware of direction: `reverse = {v: k for k, v in (link_map or {}).items() if v != SKIP and _vendor_counts[v] == 1}` (outbound_links.py:184)
link_direction.py:24 `INVERSE_RELATION: dict[str, str] = {"blocks": "depends_on", "depends_on": "blocks"}` and resolve_inbound_link applies it for inwardIssue — the override recovery bypasses this
RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK marks depends_on with swap=True (value_maps.py:106), so depends_on/blocks are two directional faces of one edge that must be disambiguated by inward/outward
advisory.finding: In _diff_link_removals, an OVERRIDDEN remote link type recovered via `reverse.get(opaque_vendor_type)` is attributed to a single fixed relation and does NOT undergo the inward/outward direction inversion that link_direction.resolve_inbound_link/INVERSE_RELATION applies for built-in types. For an asymmetric (swap=True) relation such as depends_on/blocks that is remapped to a custom vendor type, an inward vs outward remote link both recover the same relation, so the (relation, local_target) local-deps comparison and should_propagate_removal gate can match the wrong relation face — mis-removing or mis-retaining a link.
scenarios: A project remaps depends_on (or blocks) to a custom Jira link type and a managed link is deleted locally; the remote link sits on the inwardIssue side.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a _diff_links test with an override on a payloadless relation (e.g. link_map={"supersedes":"Duplicate"}) asserting the ADD emits type="Duplicate", swap=False.
evidence: outbound_links.py:57: `return (override, payload[1] if payload else False)`
value_maps.py:128 UNSYNCED_RELATIONS declares duplicates/supersedes/discovered_from/caused_by — `link_payload_for_relation` returns None for these

test_link_mapping.py override tests only use relates_to (test_link_override_changes_add_type) and depends_on (test_override_preserves_builtin_swap_for_depends_on), both of which HAVE built-in payloads; search for `supersedes`/`duplicates` in the test file returns no matches
advisory.finding: No test exercises _resolve_link's override-on-a-payloadless-relation branch: an override for a relation with no built-in payload (e.g. `duplicates`, `supersedes`, `caused_by`, `discovered_from`, all declared UNSYNCED) hits the `payload[1] if payload else False` else-branch, newly emitting an ADD with swap=False. Every override test uses relates_to/depends_on, which have built-in payloads, so this operator-facing sync-a-previously-unsynced-relation behavior is untested.
scenarios: An operator config maps `duplicates = "Duplicate"` in link_map; a dep with relation=duplicates should emit an ADD of type Duplicate with swap=False
A regression in the else-branch (e.g. returning None or the wrong swap) would silently drop or mis-emit the link
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test: ticket dep with relation="supersedes", link_map={"supersedes":"Duplicate"}, assert out == [{action:add,type:Duplicate,to_key:...,relation:supersedes,swap:False,link_uuid:...}].

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that _effective_link_map_for raises MappingConfigError on a link_map value outside declared link_types.
evidence: test_link_mapping.py test_link_undeclared_fails_closed calls only `cfg_mod.effective_link_map("REB", proj)`, not `outbound_differ._effective_link_map_for`
advisory.finding: The differ seam outbound_differ._effective_link_map_for duplicates its own fail-closed mc.validate() call (lines 343) but no test drives that seam with an out-of-vocabulary link type; only config.effective_link_map's fail-closed path is covered (test_link_undeclared_fails_closed). The two validate sites can drift.
scenarios: The differ seam's validate is removed or altered while config.effective_link_map's stays intact — the UPDATE path would stop failing closed with no test failure

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Factor the shared link-map resolution/validation into one helper parameterized by SKIP-retention so config.effective_link_map and _effective_link_map_for cannot drift.
evidence: outbound_differ.py:340-344 duplicates config.py:236-241: both build `builtin = mc.MappingLayer(link_map=config.local_to_jira_link)`, call `resolve_for_project`, then `validate(resolved, mc.Capability(has_link_types=True))`
config.effective_link_map returns `{k: v for ... if v != mc.SKIP}` while _effective_link_map_for returns `dict(resolved.link_map)` — the ONLY intended difference is SKIP retention
dropped.finding: outbound_differ._effective_link_map_for re-implements config.effective_link_map's resolve/validate pipeline (load_mapping_config -> MappingLayer(link_map=config.local_to_jira_link) -> resolve_for_project -> validate) instead of delegating to a shared helper, differing only in retaining SKIP. The two copies can drift if the resolution/validation contract changes.
scenarios: A future change to the built-in link layer or validation capability must be edited in both config.py and outbound_differ.py.
